benchmark_note: No sufficiently stable timestamped external consensus for the Sept. 11 August core-CPI release was located at the Aug. 28 evidence cutoff, so no later consensus will be retrofitted into the original forecast record.
resolution_rule: Use the first U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics CPI release published 2026-09-11 at 08:30 ET. Resolve TRUE if the seasonally adjusted August 2026 CPI excluding food and energy month-over-month change is 0.3% or higher at BLS's published precision; otherwise FALSE. Score the 0.54 probability with Brier and log loss. Score the 0.3% point estimate by absolute error and compare it with the frozen July no-change point of 0.2% and the frozen June-July two-release mean of 0.1%. Record whether the realized value lies in the 0.1%-0.4% 80% interval. Do not substitute later revisions or a later-created consensus benchmark.
rationale: H003 is the narrow leader at 0.36 versus H001 at 0.34 after Warsh's Aug. 28 speech made the current price-stability reaction function unusually explicit, while H001 remains close because oil fell sharply and medium-term inflation expectations remain broadly anchored.

Warsh said recent better summer inflation readings had not convinced him that the underlying trend had improved; that raises the probability of renewed core persistence above a pure recent-trend extrapolation.
July core CPI was only 0.2% m/m and June was 0.0%, so the model keeps the >=0.3% event only modestly above even rather than making a high-confidence inflation-reacceleration call.

Core CPI is chosen rather than headline CPI because the immediate oil/Hormuz channel weakened sharply this week; the target more directly tests H003's underlying-inflation/policy-constraint branch against H001's benign-disinflation branch.

The interval is not widened despite geopolitical uncertainty because the experiment's 80% intervals have covered every resolved interval-bearing forecast so far; preserving sharpness is part of the calibration test.
surprising_if: Core CPI is <=0.0% m/m while contemporaneous activity and labor remain resilient, materially strengthening H001's benign-disinflation branch.
Core CPI is >=0.5% m/m despite lower late-August oil, indicating much stronger underlying price persistence than the current distribution assigns.
source_notes: BLS September 2026 schedule lists the August CPI release for 2026-09-11 at 08:30 ET.
Reuters reported July core CPI +0.2% m/m and June core CPI 0.0% m/m in their respective first-release coverage.
